entries.definition: A conditional latent sequence-model family that extends a probabilistic hierarchical decision tree by coupling each decision level to the same level at the previous time.

It is not a hard deterministic classification tree, an independent-chain factorial HMM, a tree-shaped index, or a particular variational inference algorithm. Current higher-level decisions influence lower-level decisions; independent factorial chains arise only under additional restrictions. The model conditions on an external input sequence. The probabilistic hierarchy sums over decision paths; it is not necessarily a hard classification tree. Input conditioning and an output expert do not imply a causal interpretation of the graph.
Independent latent chains, a single HMM and an ordinary hierarchical mixture arise under specific restrictions, not as unconditional aliases of this family.

Forest-of-chains, forest-of-trees and point-mass inference discard different posterior dependencies. A coordinate Viterbi step finds the best path for one fixed-context chain, not a guaranteed global joint MAP path.

claims.statement: For level m and time t, its latent decision z_t^m is distributed conditional on the current input x_t, all current ancestor decisions z_t^1,...,z_t^(m-1), and its own preceding decision z_(t-1)^m. Initial decisions condition on the input and current ancestors without a preceding-time state. Multiplying these normalized conditional factors and one observation factor p(y_t|x_t,z_t^1,...,z_t^M) per time gives a normalized directed model conditional on inputs. A latent path through the hierarchy selects an output expert. Exact inference may enumerate the joint states but grows exponentially with hierarchy depth. The paper explores three distinct approximations: a product of chain-path distributions that preserves temporal dependence within each level; a product over times of tree-structured distributions that preserves current ancestor dependence; and a point-mass path approximation. Its point-mass procedure optimizes one level’s path by a Viterbi subroutine while holding the other paths fixed. These are inference choices for the family, not alternative definitions of its identity.

entries.name: Mixed memory Markov model
entries.definition: A family of compact temporal probability models whose component transition distributions are convex mixtures of transition tables indexed by a single selected predecessor lag or component.
entries.identity_notes: This record covers the mixed-memory construction of Saul and Jordan, including higher-order scalar, multicomponent first-order and hidden-state extensions. Mixed memory means a latent selector chooses one predecessor for a component distribution. It does not mean external neural memory, a mixture selecting an entire HMM, independent factorial chains, or an unrestricted full higher-order transition table. EM and coordinate Viterbi are estimation/inference procedures, not aliases for the model. limitations: A convex sum of single-predecessor effects cannot represent every higher-order interaction; for example an unrestricted XOR dependence on two binary predecessors is not additive in this way. Compact parameter counts do not establish universal expressiveness.

The displayed vector transition explicitly assumes conditional independence of current components given the previous vector. The source’s broad wording about avoiding strong conditional-independence assumptions must not override its product factorization.

Selector weights are properties of a fitted parameterization, not uniquely identified causal influence or a generally valid measure of correlation. Initial histories and observed-window boundaries must be specified when counting transitions.

In the hidden extension, exact EM needs joint posterior expectations of selectors and hidden-state indicator products. Equations (20) and (22) display hidden indicators outside the expectation, which is not a general full-posterior EM formula; clamping a path changes the calculation. Equation (17) also reverses emission arguments relative to Equation (16).

Coordinate Viterbi improves or preserves the joint path score under an exact single-chain update, but need not reach global MAP or optimize the marginal observed likelihood. Ties and stopping rules require care.

The Bach example illustrates the authors’ approximate procedure. Figure 2 uses joint path log probability, not exact marginal likelihood. No accuracy, causal discovery, training reproduction or general scaling guarantee for hidden inference is curated.

claims.statement: For a scalar k-order sequence, write p(i_t|i_(t-1),...,i_(t-k))=sum_mu psi(mu) a_mu(i_t|i_(t-mu)), with nonnegative selector weights summing to one and each transition table normalized over the current state. Given observed predecessor and current values, a selector responsibility is proportional to psi(mu) a_mu(i_t|i_(t-mu)); parameter re-estimation can use these expected selector-weighted counts. For a vector state I_t with components nu, the first-order multicomponent form is p(I_t|I_(t-1))=product_nu sum_mu psi_nu(mu) a_nu,mu(i_t^nu|i_(t-1)^mu). Thus current components are conditionally independent given the complete previous vector, despite possible marginal dependence. The hidden extension uses this transition and an emission p(J_t|I_t)=product_nu sum_mu phi_nu(mu) b_nu,mu(j_t^nu|i_t^mu). Fully observed parameter counts scale quadratically rather than exponentially in the number of components for fixed alphabet size; exact hidden posterior inference can still be exponential. The paper instead illustrates a coordinate Viterbi approximation that fixes other hidden chains while optimizing one chain path.

claims.statement: In the linear categorical case, for fixed length L and inverse temperature beta, assign joint probability proportional to exp(beta[Pi_(s_1)+sum_(t=1)^(L-1) A_(s_t,s_(t+1))+sum_(t=1)^L B_(s_t,y_t)]), normalized over all hidden paths and observation sequences by Z_L. A and B are tied across time and need not themselves be log-normalized transition or emission probabilities. Observed likelihood is the ratio of a clamped and a free partition function. A log-likelihood derivative with respect to a tied interaction is beta times its expected count under the clamped distribution minus its expected count under the free distribution. For the selected tractable graphs, exact variable elimination computes these quantities: pruning sums out leaves, decimation sums over an intermediate state, and parallel interactions combine additively in the energy. The paper uses particular coupled chains at different time resolutions and selected loops that preserve an eliminable structure; tractability depends on intermediate state-space size, not merely the presence of temporal edges.

claims.statement: For fixed model parameters and observations, choose q(S)=product_m q_m(s_1:T^m) and optimize the evidence lower bound E_q[log p(Y,S)-log q(S)], equivalently minimizing KL(q||p(S|Y)). Each chain factor is globally normalized over its path and retains the model’s initial and transition factors multiplied by positive unary potentials h_t^m. In the additive Gaussian model, h_t^m is proportional to exp((W_m)^T C^-1 [y_t-sum_(l!=m) W_l E_q[s_t^l]] - 0.5 diag((W_m)^T C^-1 W_m)), componentwise over the chain’s states. With other chain factors fixed, run forward–backward using these unary factors to update that chain’s state and temporal-pair moments, then repeat across chains. Same-time moments between different chains factorize under q; within-chain temporal moments do not. Such exact single-chain coordinate updates increase or preserve the bound for fixed model parameters. The moments may also supply a variational E-step for model fitting, but this approximate posterior does not become the exact posterior merely by convergence.

source_analysis.mapping_assessment: Seventeen exact fully annotated AIO nodes and all63 semantic label/synonym hits were inspected. Fourteen generated YAMLs were byte-verified after prior full reading and three freshly read. Six native neighbors were read in this or the immediately preceding cohort. HMDT and mixed-memory models are finite directed conditional factorizations with broader BayesianNetwork mappings. HMDT has a related DecisionTree mapping: the AIO target is classification-scoped, while the sequence model need not classify. Mixed-memory models have a related MarkovChain mapping because higher-order scalar and hidden observed processes need not be first-order. Boltzmann chains have a broad BoltzmannMachineNetwork mapping and related MarkovChain association qualified by linear topology and terminal factors. RestrictedBoltzmannMachine lacks the temporal hidden-hidden interactions of the source construction, despite its broad abbreviated definition. ProbabilisticGraphicalModel and MachineLearningTask are task-scoped; TrainingStrategy is preprocessing-scoped. CausalGraphicalModel adds assumptions not supplied by a dependence graph. MixtureofExpertsLLM, MemoryAugmentedLLM, EnergyBasedLLM and ImplicitLanguageModel are language-specific; no generic identity is inferred from related synonyms. MemoryCellLayer and ProbabilisticHiddenLayer are components, not these models. ProbabilisticTopicModel is text/topic-specific. RecurrentNeuralNetwork is not forced as a generic parent of tabular probabilistic models. Native HMM, FHMM, IOHMM, PoHMM, structured FHMM inference and EM distinguish model structures, parameterizations and procedures; their context inspection is not renewed scientific approval.
